name: Wraps and Tacos
summary: Corn tortillas and whole-wheat wraps filled with things you would actually want for dinner: chicken tinga, cod with lime slaw, lentil-walnut tacos, cumin-lime trout, Korean-style beef and salmon enchiladas. Vegetables or fruit at every breakfast, lunch and dinner, and beans, lentils or chickpeas every day.
howItWorks:
**Tortillas as the plate, not the meal.** Corn tortillas and whole-wheat wraps carry fillings that do the real work: beans, lentils, fish, chicken, lean beef, eggs and plenty of vegetables. Cheese is a sprinkle, canned beans are no-salt-added, and each tortilla is a sensible portion so the week stays under the sodium ceiling.

**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday's chicken tinga, Wednesday's lentil-walnut tacos, Friday's Korean-style beef and Saturday's salmon enchiladas each make two portions, so the next lunch is done. Cool each pot within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep the tortillas and fresh toppings separate, and reheat the filling until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F). Wash all fruit and vegetables before cutting, limes too.

**Fish and protein.** Canned salmon on Monday, cumin-lime trout on Thursday and salmon enchiladas on Saturday bring omega-3 and some **vitamin D**. Cod on Tuesday is lean and iodine-rich. Chicken, beef, eggs, lentils, pinto and black beans and chickpeas cover the rest. Fresh fish is bought and cooked within a day; an opened tin is covered and used within 2 days.

**What changes at Light.** Light drops the second snack each day and makes lighter dishes: fewer beans and lentils, less oil and avocado, more spinach. Fish, chicken and beef stay a full portion, as they carry much of the protein, zinc and **vitamin D**. Tacos take one and a half to two and a half small corn tortillas. Egg breakfasts have two eggs at 1,400 and 1,600, three at 1,800.

**Bigger days.** Big adds a snack each day, with beans, nuts or fruit, and grows the chicken, beef, fish, beans and lentils. Tortillas grow toward the top of the range, Friday's egg breakfast goes to three eggs, and the beans on the side get a bigger scoop.

recipes.name: Sweet potato, egg and salsa verde breakfast tacos
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican huevos con papas and breakfast tacos
recipes.about: Grated sweet potato crisped with cumin, wilted spinach, black beans and firm scrambled eggs, tucked into warm corn tortillas with salsa verde and sliced avocado, with a glass of milk on the side. The sweet potato brings **vitamin A and fibre**, the eggs and beans bring protein and choline, and the milk brings calcium.
steps: Wash the sweet potato, spinach and avocado. Grate the sweet potato on the coarse side of a grater and slice the avocado.

Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the sweet potato with the cumin, stirring now and then, until tender with golden edges, about 4 minutes. Add the spinach and beans and stir until the spinach wilts and the beans are hot, about 1 minute.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper and pour them in. Stir gently until the eggs are completely set, with no liquid left and the yolks firm, about 3 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side. Spoon in the eggs and top with the salsa verde and avocado.
recipes.tip: Grate the sweet potato the night before and keep it covered in the fridge to save a few minutes.

recipes.name: Mixed berry overnight oats with walnuts and sunflower seeds
recipes.about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt with frozen berries, cinnamon and a scatter of toasted walnuts. The oats bring **fibre**, the berries bring vitamin C, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3, with sunflower seeds for vitamin E.
steps: Stir the oats, yogurt, cinnamon and enough of the milk to cover the oats well in a jar or bowl. Stir in the frozen berries, cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
In the morning, toast the walnuts and sunflower seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until they smell nutty, about 2 minutes.
Stir the oats, pour over the rest of the milk (or drink it alongside) and scatter the toasted walnuts and seeds over the top. Eat it cold.
recipes.tip: Make two jars at once and keep them covered in the fridge. Eat soaked oats within 3 days, and make a fresh batch after that. If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

recipes.name: Banana and peanut butter breakfast wrap with orange
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a peanut butter and banana sandwich
recipes.about: A warm whole-wheat tortilla with peanut butter, sliced banana, a spoonful of Greek yogurt and cinnamon, with an orange and a glass of milk on the side. The peanut butter, yogurt and milk bring **protein and calcium**, and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into wedges. Peel and slice the banana.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side so it turns soft and a little toasty.

Spread the peanut butter over the tortilla, lay the banana down the middle, spoon on the yogurt, sprinkle with the sunflower seeds and dust with cinnamon. Roll it up and eat it with the orange and the milk.
recipes.tip: Warm the peanut butter for 10 seconds if it is stiff, so it spreads easily.

recipes.name: Chipotle salmon salad wrap with black beans and crunchy veg
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic salmon salad sandwich, with chipotle and black beans
recipes.about: Canned salmon mashed with Greek yogurt, lime and a little chipotle, rolled in a whole-wheat tortilla with black beans, red pepper, carrot and spinach. Canned salmon with its soft bones brings **omega-3, vitamin D and calcium**, and the red pepper brings vitamin C.

ingredients.note: minced, with a little of the sauce

steps: Wash the pepper, carrot, spinach and cilantro. Dice the pepper, grate the carrot and chop the cilantro.
In a bowl, mash the salmon with the yogurt, chipotle, lime juice, cilantro and pepper until it holds together. Fold in the beans, pepper and carrot.
Lay the spinach down the middle of the tortilla, spoon the salmon mixture on top, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
If you are packing it, wrap it well and keep it in a cold bag with an ice pack, and eat it the same day. Cover and refrigerate any opened tin and use it within 2 days.
recipes.tip: Chipotle varies a lot from tin to tin. Start with half and taste.

recipes.name: Peanut-lime chicken and crunchy cabbage wrap
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Thai peanut salad and Vietnamese rice paper rolls
recipes.about: Thin strips of seared chicken breast tossed with shredded cabbage, carrot and cucumber in a peanut, lime and soy dressing, rolled into a whole-wheat tortilla. The chicken brings **lean protein and niacin**, and the lime and crunchy raw vegetables keep it bright.
steps: Wash the cabbage, carrot, cucumber and cilantro. Shred the cabbage, grate the carrot and cut the cucumber into thin sticks.

Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with the cumin and cook, turning now and then, until golden and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes. Put it on a clean plate, then wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Whisk the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, garlic and chili powder with a spoonful of warm water until smooth and pourable.

Toss the chicken, cabbage, carrot, cucumber and cilantro with the dressing. Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side, pile the filling down the middle, scatter the sunflower seeds over it, fold in the sides and roll up.
If you are packing it, keep it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
recipes.tip: Slice the chicken across the grain, as thin as you can, so it cooks quickly and stays tender.

recipes.name: Smoky black bean and pepper tacos with lime yogurt
recipes.about: Black beans mashed lightly with sweet pepper, onion, cumin and smoked paprika, piled into warm corn tortillas with spinach, avocado and a cool lime and cilantro yogurt. The beans bring **fibre, folate and iron**, and the lime yogurt brings calcium.
steps: Wash the pepper, spinach, cilantro and avocado. Slice the pepper, onion and avocado.
Warm the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the pepper and onion until soft and a little charred at the edges, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika for 30 seconds.

Add the beans with a splash of water and the salt. Cook, mashing about a third of them with the back of a spoon, until thick and hot all the way through, about 4 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Stir the yogurt with the lime juice and cilantro. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, then fill them with the beans, avocado, a spoonful of the yogurt and a little crumbled queso fresco, and scatter the sunflower seeds over the top.
recipes.tip: Mash a few more of the beans if you like the filling thicker.

recipes.name: Chicken tinga tacos with pinto beans and lime-pickled onion
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by tinga de pollo from Puebla, with beans stretching the chicken
recipes.about: Tender chicken breast simmered in a smoky chipotle and tomato sauce, shredded and stirred with pinto beans and spinach, then piled into warm corn tortillas with lime-pickled onion, grated carrot, cilantro and avocado. The chicken and beans make it **filling, with fibre and folate**, and the tomato, spinach and lime bring vitamin C.

ingredients.note: minced, with a little of the sauce

steps: Wash the carrot, spinach, cilantro and avocado. Slice the onion and grate the carrot. Put a small handful of the onion slices in a bowl with half the lime juice and a pinch of the salt to quick-pickle while you cook. Chop the garlic and spinach.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the rest of the onion until soft and golden at the edges, about 7 minutes, then stir in the garlic, oregano and cumin for 30 seconds.

Add the tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon, then the chipotle and the rest of the lime juice. Bring to a simmer and nestle in the chicken. Cover and cook, turning once, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part, about 15 minutes.

Lift the chicken onto a clean plate and shred it with two forks. Wash your hands, the board and the forks after handling the raw chicken. Return the chicken to the pan with the beans, spinach and the rest of the salt and simmer until the spinach wilts and the sauce is thick and spoonable, about 4 minutes.
Toss the carrot with the cilantro. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, then fill them with the tinga, carrot, pickled onion and avocado.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion of tinga within 1 hour in a shallow container, then cover and refrigerate it with the carrot, pickled onion and tortillas kept separate. Use it within 3 days and reheat the tinga until steaming, to 74 °C.
recipes.tip: The tinga freezes well without the tortillas and toppings: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C. For less heat, use half the chipotle.

recipes.name: Pan-seared cod tacos with lime-cabbage slaw and black beans
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Baja-style fish tacos
recipes.about: Chili-and-cumin cod seared in a hot pan and flaked into warm corn tortillas with a crunchy lime and cilantro cabbage slaw and a quick avocado-lime crema, with garlicky black beans on the side. Cod is a **lean, low-fat protein with iodine**, and the beans bring fibre and folate.
steps: Wash the cabbage, carrot, cilantro and avocado. Toss the cabbage, carrot, half the cilantro and half the lime juice with a pinch of the salt and a pinch of chili.
Mash the avocado with the rest of the lime juice and cilantro into a loose crema.

Pat the cod dry and rub it with half the oil, the chili powder, cumin and the rest of the salt. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the cod 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Warm the beans in a small pot with the garlic and the remaining oil and a splash of water until steaming hot. Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until golden, about 2 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Flake the cod into them, top with the slaw, crema, queso fresco and sunflower seeds, and serve the beans on the side.
recipes.tip: Buy fresh cod and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight. Haddock or pollock works the same way.

recipes.name: Lentil-walnut tacos with lime crema
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by walnut "taco meat"
recipes.about: A smoky, meaty-textured filling of lentils and toasted walnuts, spiced with cumin and paprika and cooked with tomato, spooned into corn tortillas with shredded lettuce and a lime yogurt crema. The lentils bring **fibre, iron and folate**, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the lettuce, spinach and cilantro. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 3 minutes, then chop them finely.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 7 minutes, then stir in the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, chili and oregano for 30 seconds.

Add the lentils, tomatoes with their juice and the soy sauce. Cook, mashing about half the lentils with the back of a spoon, until thick and hot all the way through, about 8 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then the walnuts.
Stir the yogurt with half the lime juice and half the cilantro. Shred the lettuce and toss it with the rest of the lime juice and cilantro.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill them with the lentil mixture, lettuce and crema.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion of filling within 1 hour in a shallow container, then cover and refrigerate it with the lettuce, crema and tortillas kept separate. Use it within 3 days and reheat the filling until steaming, to 74 °C.
recipes.tip: The filling freezes well without the crema and lettuce: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C.

recipes.name: Cumin-lime trout tacos with pineapple salsa
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Baja fish tacos and pineapple salsa
recipes.about: Cumin and lime-rubbed trout seared until flaky and piled into warm corn tortillas with a juicy pineapple and red pepper salsa, crunchy cabbage and toasted sunflower seeds. Trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the pineapple and pepper bring vitamin C.
steps: Wash the pineapple, pepper, cabbage and cilantro. Toss the pineapple, onion, pepper, cilantro and two thirds of the lime juice with a pinch of the salt.

Pat the trout dry and rub it with the oil, cumin, chili powder, the rest of the lime juice and the remaining salt. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the trout 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until golden, about 2 minutes. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side.
Flake the trout into the tortillas with the cabbage, a big spoonful of salsa, the queso fresco and the toasted seeds.
recipes.tip: Buy fresh trout and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight. Slice any leftover pineapple for tomorrow's snack.

recipes.name: Korean-style beef lettuce and tortilla wraps
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean ssam and bulgogi flavours
recipes.about: Gochujang-glazed lean beef with garlic and wilted spinach, folded into warm corn tortillas with butter lettuce leaves and a crunchy lime-pickled carrot and cucumber. The beef brings **iron and zinc** and the pickled vegetables bring crunch and brightness.

ingredients.note: washed and cut in thin sticks
washed and cut in thin sticks

steps: Wash the carrot, cucumber, spinach, lettuce and ginger. Cut the carrot and cucumber into thin sticks and toss them with the lime juice and the pepper. Let them sit while you cook.
Stir the gochujang, soy sauce, garlic and ginger with a splash of water into a loose paste.

Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through to 71 °C (160 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
Stir in the paste and the spinach and cook until the spinach wilts and the beef is glazed, about 2 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Lay a lettuce leaf on each, add the beef and top with the pickled vegetables. Fold and eat.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion of beef within 1 hour in a shallow container, cover and refrigerate it with the pickles, lettuce and tortilla kept separate. Use it within 3 days and reheat the beef until steaming, to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Gochujang brands vary in heat and salt, so taste the paste first. Use less for a milder wrap.

recipes.name: Salmon, pinto bean and spinach enchiladas verdes
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican enchiladas verdes, with canned salmon for the filling
recipes.about: Corn tortillas rolled around a filling of flaked canned salmon, pinto beans and wilted spinach, covered in a tangy salsa verde and tomato sauce and baked until bubbling, then finished with avocado and cilantro. The salmon, with its soft bones, brings **omega-3, vitamin D and calcium**, and the beans bring fibre.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Wash the spinach, cilantro and avocado. Chop the onion and spinach.

Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cumin, then the beans, spinach and salt, and cook until the spinach wilts and the beans are hot, about 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and fold in the salmon, flaking it with a fork.

Stir the salsa verde with the tomatoes, crushed with a spoon, to make the sauce. Spread a thin layer of it over the bottom of a baking dish. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan so they bend without cracking, fill each with some of the salmon mixture, roll them up and set them seam side down in the dish.
Pour the rest of the sauce over the top, cover the dish with foil and bake until bubbling at the edges and hot all the way through, to 74 °C (165 °F), about 25 minutes.

Top with avocado and cilantro. This makes two portions. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, refrigerate it, and use it within 3 days. Reheat until steaming, to 74 °C. Cover and refrigerate any opened tin and use it within 2 days.
recipes.tip: Freeze the baked enchiladas without the avocado: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C.

recipes.name: Chili-lime roasted cauliflower and chickpea tacos with caramelized pineapple
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by the chili and pineapple flavours of Mexico City taco stands
recipes.about: Cauliflower and chickpeas roasted in a smoky chili, lime and tomato rub with caramelized pineapple, tucked into corn tortillas with a lime yogurt crema, raw onion and sunflower seeds. The chickpeas and cauliflower bring **fibre, folate and plant protein**, and the pineapple brings vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a tray with parchment. Wash the cauliflower, pineapple and cilantro.

Whisk the tomatoes, half the lime juice, the oil, garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano and salt in a large bowl. Add the cauliflower, chickpeas and half the onion and toss until coated.

Spread everything in a single layer on the tray, using two trays if it is crowded, so the chickpeas roast rather than steam. Roast for 12 minutes. Add the pineapple wedges and roast until the cauliflower is tender and charred at the edges and the pineapple is caramelized, about 10 minutes more.
Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until golden, about 2 minutes. Stir the yogurt with the rest of the lime juice.

Chop the roasted cauliflower and pineapple roughly. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill them with the roasted mixture, a spoonful of crema, the remaining raw onion, cilantro and the sunflower seeds.

recipes.name: Orange with sunflower seeds
recipes.about: A juicy orange with a small handful of sunflower seeds. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the seeds bring vitamin E and magnesium.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into wedges. Eat it with the sunflower seeds.

recipes.name: Apple slices with walnuts
recipes.about: Crisp apple slices with a handful of walnuts. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3** and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, core it and cut it into slices. Eat it with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Carrot, cucumber and pepper sticks with lime and chili
recipes.about: Crunchy raw vegetables with a squeeze of lime and a shake of chili, the way street vendors serve them. They bring **vitamins A and C** and almost no calories.
steps: Wash the carrot, cucumber and pepper and cut them into sticks and strips.
Squeeze the lime over them and shake on the chili powder and salt.

recipes.name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
recipes.about: A banana with a handful of walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. The banana brings **potassium** and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Peel the banana and eat it with the walnuts, dusted with the cinnamon.

recipes.name: Orange with walnuts
recipes.about: A juicy orange with a handful of walnuts. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into wedges. Eat it with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Pineapple with lime and walnuts
recipes.about: Juicy pineapple chunks with a squeeze of lime and a handful of walnuts. The pineapple brings **vitamin C and manganese** and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the pineapple, peel it and cut it into chunks, then squeeze the lime over it.
Scatter the walnuts over the top and eat.

recipes.name: Lime-chili roasted chickpeas
recipes.about: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with lime, chili and cumin. The chickpeas bring **protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (410 °F). Rinse the chickpeas and dry them very well on a clean towel.
Toss them with the oil, chili powder, cumin and salt and roast on a tray, shaking once, until crisp, about 25 minutes. Squeeze the lime over them and let them cool, as they crisp more as they cool.
recipes.tip: Roast a double batch and keep them uncovered at room temperature for up to 2 days.

recipes.name: Warm edamame with lime and chili
recipes.about: Edamame beans warmed through with lime and a pinch of chili. The edamame brings **protein, iron and folate**.
steps: Cook the edamame in boiling water until steaming hot and tender, about 4 minutes, then drain.
Toss with the lime juice, chili powder and salt and eat warm.

recipes.name: Banana with peanut butter
recipes.about: A banana with a spoonful of peanut butter. The banana brings **potassium** and the peanut butter brings protein and vitamin E.
steps: Peel and slice the banana and eat it with the peanut butter.

recipes.name: Black bean and lime dip with pepper and cucumber sticks
recipes.about: A smooth black bean dip with lime and cumin, with pepper and cucumber sticks for dipping. The beans bring **fibre, iron and protein**.
steps: Wash the pepper and cucumber and cut them into strips and sticks.
Mash the beans with the lime juice, oil, cumin and salt, adding a spoonful of water until smooth.
Serve the dip with the vegetables. Keep any leftover dip covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.

recipes.name: Crunchy cumin pinto beans
recipes.about: Oven-crisped pinto beans with cumin, smoked paprika and a squeeze of lime. The beans bring **protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (410 °F). Rinse the pinto beans and dry them very well on a clean towel.

Toss them with the oil, cumin, smoked paprika and salt and roast on a tray, shaking once, until crisp at the edges, about 25 minutes. Squeeze the lime over them and let them cool, as they crisp more as they cool.
recipes.tip: Roast a double batch and keep them uncovered at room temperature for up to 2 days.

recipes.name: Lime and cumin chickpea dip with carrot and cucumber sticks
recipes.about: A quick, chunky chickpea dip with lime, garlic and cumin, with carrot and cucumber sticks for dipping. The chickpeas bring **protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Wash the carrot and cucumber and cut them into sticks.
Mash the chickpeas with the lime juice, oil, garlic, cumin and salt, adding a spoonful of water until you have a chunky dip.
Serve the dip with the sticks. Keep any leftover dip covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.

The chicken and beans make it **filling, with fibre and folate**, and the tomato, spinach and lime bring vitamin C.

ingredients.note: minced, with a little of the sauce

steps: Wash the carrot, spinach, cilantro and avocado. Slice the onion and grate the carrot. Put a small handful of the onion slices in a bowl with half the lime juice and a pinch of the salt to quick-pickle while you cook. Chop the garlic and spinach.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the rest of the onion until soft and golden at the edges, about 7 minutes, then stir in the garlic, oregano and cumin for 30 seconds.

Add the tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon, then the chipotle and the rest of the lime juice. Bring to a simmer and nestle in the chicken. Cover and cook, turning once, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part, about 15 minutes.

Lift the chicken onto a clean plate and shred it with two forks. Wash your hands, the board and the forks after handling the raw chicken. Return the chicken to the pan with the beans, spinach and the rest of the salt and simmer until the spinach wilts and the sauce is thick and spoonable, about 4 minutes.
Toss the carrot with the cilantro. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, then fill them with the tinga, carrot, pickled onion and avocado.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion of tinga within 1 hour in a shallow container, then cover and refrigerate it with the carrot, pickled onion and tortillas kept separate. Use it within 3 days and reheat the tinga until steaming, to 74 °C.
recipes.tip: The tinga freezes well without the tortillas and toppings: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C. For less heat, use half the chipotle.

recipes.name: Pan-seared cod tacos with lime-cabbage slaw and black beans
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Baja-style fish tacos
recipes.about: Chili-and-cumin cod seared in a hot pan and flaked into warm corn tortillas with a crunchy lime and cilantro cabbage slaw and a quick avocado-lime crema, with garlicky black beans on the side. Cod is a **lean, low-fat protein with iodine**, and the beans bring fibre and folate.
steps: Wash the cabbage, carrot, cilantro and avocado. Toss the cabbage, carrot, half the cilantro and half the lime juice with a pinch of the salt and a pinch of chili.
Mash the avocado with the rest of the lime juice and cilantro into a loose crema.

Pat the cod dry and rub it with half the oil, the chili powder, cumin and the rest of the salt. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the cod 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Warm the beans in a small pot with the garlic and the remaining oil and a splash of water until steaming hot. Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until golden, about 2 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Flake the cod into them, top with the slaw, crema, queso fresco and sunflower seeds, and serve the beans on the side.
recipes.tip: Buy fresh cod and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight. Haddock or pollock works the same way.

recipes.name: Lentil-walnut tacos with lime crema
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by walnut "taco meat"
recipes.about: A smoky, meaty-textured filling of lentils and toasted walnuts, spiced with cumin and paprika and cooked with tomato, spooned into corn tortillas with shredded lettuce and a lime yogurt crema. The lentils bring **fibre, iron and folate**, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the lettuce, spinach and cilantro. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 3 minutes, then chop them finely.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 7 minutes, then stir in the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, chili and oregano for 30 seconds.

Add the lentils, tomatoes with their juice and the soy sauce. Cook, mashing about half the lentils with the back of a spoon, until thick and hot all the way through, about 8 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then the walnuts.
Stir the yogurt with half the lime juice and half the cilantro. Shred the lettuce and toss it with the rest of the lime juice and cilantro.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill them with the lentil mixture, lettuce and crema.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion of filling within 1 hour in a shallow container, then cover and refrigerate it with the lettuce, crema and tortillas kept separate. Use it within 3 days and reheat the filling until steaming, to 74 °C.
recipes.tip: The filling freezes well without the crema and lettuce: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C.

recipes.name: Cumin-lime trout tacos with pineapple salsa
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Baja fish tacos and pineapple salsa
recipes.about: Cumin and lime-rubbed trout seared until flaky and piled into warm corn tortillas with a juicy pineapple and red pepper salsa, crunchy cabbage and toasted sunflower seeds. Trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the pineapple and pepper bring vitamin C.
steps: Wash the pineapple, pepper, cabbage and cilantro. Toss the pineapple, onion, pepper, cilantro and two thirds of the lime juice with a pinch of the salt.

Pat the trout dry and rub it with the oil, cumin, chili powder, the rest of the lime juice and the remaining salt. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the trout 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until golden, about 2 minutes. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side.
Flake the trout into the tortillas with the cabbage, a big spoonful of salsa, the queso fresco and the toasted seeds.
recipes.tip: Buy fresh trout and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight. Slice any leftover pineapple for tomorrow's snack.

recipes.name: Smoky black bean and pepper tacos with lime yogurt
recipes.about: Black beans mashed lightly with sweet pepper, onion, cumin and smoked paprika, piled into warm corn tortillas with spinach, avocado and a cool lime and cilantro yogurt. The beans bring **fibre, folate and iron**, and the lime yogurt brings calcium.
steps: Wash the pepper, spinach, cilantro and avocado. Slice the pepper, onion and avocado.
Warm the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the pepper and onion until soft and a little charred at the edges, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika for 30 seconds.

Add the beans with a splash of water and the salt. Cook, mashing about a third of them with the back of a spoon, until thick and hot all the way through, about 4 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Stir the yogurt with the lime juice and cilantro. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, then fill them with the beans, avocado, a spoonful of the yogurt and a little crumbled queso fresco, and scatter the sunflower seeds over the top.
recipes.tip: Mash a few more of the beans if you like the filling thicker.

recipes.name: Korean-style beef lettuce and tortilla wraps
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean ssam and bulgogi flavours
recipes.about: Gochujang-glazed lean beef with garlic and wilted spinach, folded into warm corn tortillas with butter lettuce leaves and a crunchy lime-pickled carrot and cucumber. The beef brings **iron and zinc** and the pickled vegetables bring crunch and brightness.

ingredients.note: washed and cut in thin sticks
washed and cut in thin sticks

steps: Wash the carrot, cucumber, spinach, lettuce and ginger. Cut the carrot and cucumber into thin sticks and toss them with the lime juice and the pepper. Let them sit while you cook.
Stir the gochujang, soy sauce, garlic and ginger with a splash of water into a loose paste.

Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through to 71 °C (160 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
Stir in the paste and the spinach and cook until the spinach wilts and the beef is glazed, about 2 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Lay a lettuce leaf on each, add the beef and top with the pickled vegetables. Fold and eat.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion of beef within 1 hour in a shallow container, cover and refrigerate it with the pickles, lettuce and tortilla kept separate. Use it within 3 days and reheat the beef until steaming, to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Gochujang brands vary in heat and salt, so taste the paste first. Use less for a milder wrap.

recipes.name: Salmon, pinto bean and spinach enchiladas verdes
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican enchiladas verdes, with canned salmon for the filling
recipes.about: Corn tortillas rolled around a filling of flaked canned salmon, pinto beans and wilted spinach, covered in a tangy salsa verde and tomato sauce and baked until bubbling, then finished with avocado and cilantro. The salmon, with its soft bones, brings **omega-3, vitamin D and calcium**, and the beans bring fibre.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Wash the spinach, cilantro and avocado. Chop the onion and spinach.

Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cumin, then the beans, spinach and salt, and cook until the spinach wilts and the beans are hot, about 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and fold in the salmon, flaking it with a fork.

Stir the salsa verde with the tomatoes, crushed with a spoon, to make the sauce. Spread a thin layer of it over the bottom of a baking dish. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan so they bend without cracking, fill each with some of the salmon mixture, roll them up and set them seam side down in the dish.
Pour the rest of the sauce over the top, cover the dish with foil and bake until bubbling at the edges and hot all the way through, to 74 °C (165 °F), about 25 minutes.

Top with avocado and cilantro. This makes two portions. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, refrigerate it, and use it within 3 days. Reheat until steaming, to 74 °C. Cover and refrigerate any opened tin and use it within 2 days.
recipes.tip: Freeze the baked enchiladas without the avocado: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C.

recipes.name: Chili-lime roasted cauliflower and chickpea tacos with caramelized pineapple
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by the chili and pineapple flavours of Mexico City taco stands
recipes.about: Cauliflower and chickpeas roasted in a smoky chili, lime and tomato rub with caramelized pineapple, tucked into corn tortillas with a lime yogurt crema, raw onion and sunflower seeds. The chickpeas and cauliflower bring **fibre, folate and plant protein**, and the pineapple brings vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a tray with parchment. Wash the cauliflower, pineapple and cilantro.

Whisk the tomatoes, half the lime juice, the oil, garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano and salt in a large bowl. Add the cauliflower, chickpeas and half the onion and toss until coated.

Spread everything in a single layer on the tray, using two trays if it is crowded, so the chickpeas roast rather than steam. Roast for 12 minutes. Add the pineapple wedges and roast until the cauliflower is tender and charred at the edges and the pineapple is caramelized, about 10 minutes more.
Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until golden, about 2 minutes. Stir the yogurt with the rest of the lime juice.

Chop the roasted cauliflower and pineapple roughly. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill them with the roasted mixture, a spoonful of crema, the remaining raw onion, cilantro and the sunflower seeds.

recipes.name: Orange with sunflower seeds
recipes.about: A juicy orange with a small handful of sunflower seeds. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the seeds bring vitamin E and magnesium.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into wedges. Eat it with the sunflower seeds.

recipes.name: Pineapple with lime and walnuts
recipes.about: Juicy pineapple chunks with a squeeze of lime and a handful of walnuts. The pineapple brings **vitamin C and manganese** and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the pineapple, peel it and cut it into chunks, then squeeze the lime over it.
Scatter the walnuts over the top and eat.

recipes.name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
recipes.about: A banana with a handful of walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. The banana brings **potassium** and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Peel the banana and eat it with the walnuts, dusted with the cinnamon.

recipes.name: Black bean and lime dip with pepper and cucumber sticks
recipes.about: A smooth black bean dip with lime and cumin, with pepper and cucumber sticks for dipping. The beans bring **fibre, iron and protein**.
steps: Wash the pepper and cucumber and cut them into strips and sticks.
Mash the beans with the lime juice, oil, cumin and salt, adding a spoonful of water until smooth.
Serve the dip with the vegetables. Keep any leftover dip covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.
